what_its_for: This medicine helps lower your cholesterol and fats (triglycerides) in your blood. It works in two ways: one part (ezetimibe) blocks cholesterol from being absorbed in your intestines, and the other part (simvastatin) reduces the amount of cholesterol your liver makes. Together, they help lower your 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) and reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Take it in the evening or at bedtime, since your body makes the most cholesterol at night. Do not crush or chew the tablet. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel well — high cholesterol usually has no symptoms.
dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet (10 mg/20 mg) once daily in the evening. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your cholesterol levels and how well you respond. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor. The maximum dose is 10 mg/80 mg per day, but the 80 mg simvastatin dose is rarely used due to higher risk of muscle problems.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it is still the same evening, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time that evening. Do NOT take two doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice (more than 1 quart per day) as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can increase your risk of liver problems. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, especially antibiotics like erythromycin or clarithromycin, antifungals like fluconazole or itraconazole, certain HIV medicines, niacin (at doses above 1 gram), blood thinners like warfarin, and cyclosporine, as these can interact seriously with this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or dark brown urine — this could be a serious muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); unusual tiredness or loss of appetite; memory problems or confusion; numbness or tingling. Also tell your doctor if you become pregnant, are planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding, as this medicine must be stopped.
when_it_works: You may start to see lower cholesterol levels on blood tests within 2 to 4 weeks of starting this medicine. However, it works best when combined with a heart-healthy diet, regular exercise, and not smoking. This is a long-term medicine — most people need to take it for the rest of their life to keep their cholesterol under control.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine, and stop it immediately if you become pregnant. Older adults (65+): Use with caution, as older adults may be at higher risk for muscle problems. Children: This medicine is not approved for children under 10 years of age. Kidney or liver disease: This medicine may not be safe for people with active liver disease or severely reduced kidney function. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
